chapter: Los Angeles scene and the Ellington sound
title: Blue Light becomes Transbluency
summary: Brown tells again how his unplanned theme on Blue Light was lifted by Ellington for Transbluency and who gets credit.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: 'Transbluecency', was she on 'Transbluecency'?

I really don't remember her on Transbluecency, but 'Transbluecency' itself was a development from a tune called 'Blue Light.' 'Blue Light was a tonal poem, and to show you how the different people, or the different members would contribute to different numbers, the tonal poem was going along until in the final part Ellington looked over at me and pointed and said, 'Take one,' I mean just to take one, you know, take the chorus.

Now this was a complete surprise. I had never paid any attention to fitting into this particular piece, and all of a sudden, from the chordings and the progress that had gone ahead, this theme came to my mind, and I -- to all of our surprises, I played this theme that no one had ever heard, not even me. (Laughs.) And that is 'Blue Light.' That was the end of 'Blue Light.'

Now this theme was so prominent on the record that Ellington took it and created another number called 'Transbluecency,' and that's the way a whole lot of numbers were developed from one to the other, parts of this, parts of that, but that
